stages.title: Programming fundamentals and implementation
stages.teaches: Reading input exactly, simulating what a statement describes, and handling strings and loops without off-by-one mistakes. Most early problems are won or lost here: the idea is simple and the work is turning it into correct code.
stages.practise: Fast, careful implementation of simple statements, and trying every case when the input is small.

stages.title: Complexity analysis
stages.teaches: Estimating how many operations a solution performs before writing it, so you can tell from the limits whether O(n^2) is fine or O(n log n) is needed. It also covers integer sizes: when a product needs a 64-bit type.
stages.practise: For every problem, state the time complexity and check it against the limits before coding.

stages.title: Maths foundations
stages.teaches: Integer arithmetic, parity, rounding with integer division, and turning a description into a formula instead of a simulation.
stages.practise: Problems where a short derivation replaces a loop.

stages.title: Sorting and greedy choices
stages.teaches: Sorting to expose structure, then making the locally best choice and arguing why it is never worse than any other choice. The argument matters as much as the code.
stages.practise: Write down why the greedy choice is safe before submitting.

stages.title: Prefix sums and two pointers
stages.teaches: Answering range-sum questions in O(1) after O(n) preparation, and moving two indices through sorted data so that a nested loop becomes linear.
stages.practise: Rewrite an O(n^2) pair or subarray search as a single pass.

stages.title: Binary search
stages.teaches: Searching sorted data in O(log n), and the more powerful form: binary searching on the answer when a yes/no check is monotonic.
stages.practise: Identify the monotonic predicate first, then the boundaries.

stages.title: Data structures
stages.teaches: Choosing the right container: maps and sets for counting and lookup, stacks and queues for order, and priority queues for repeated best-element access.
stages.practise: Ask which operations the problem repeats, then pick the structure that makes them cheap.

stages.title: Number theory and combinatorics
stages.teaches: Divisibility, gcd, primes and modular arithmetic, and counting arrangements without listing them.
stages.practise: Small cases by hand, then a formula, then modular arithmetic for large answers.

stages.title: Dynamic programming
stages.teaches: Defining a state, a transition and a base case so that each subproblem is solved once. It turns exponential searches into polynomial ones.
stages.practise: Name the state in words before writing any code.

stages.title: Graphs: BFS, DFS and shortest paths
stages.teaches: Modelling a problem as nodes and edges, exploring it with BFS and DFS, and finding shortest paths and connected components.
stages.practise: Draw the graph for the sample before coding the traversal.

stages.title: Trees and advanced topics
stages.teaches: Rooted trees, subtree computations and tree DP, then structures that start to appear on the way to 1800, such as disjoint set union, segment trees and lowest common ancestors.
stages.practise: One new technique at a time, each with a few problems before moving on.
